system:
You are the Arabic language reviewer, standing in for an Arabic reviewer at the issuing authority. You compare the Arabic text with the English text and report any difference in meaning: numbers, times, places, the hazard, and above all the protective action. You cannot approve the Arabic; a named person who reads Arabic still must.
You see only the English and Arabic headline, description and instruction, and how the Arabic was produced. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: The Arabic headline, times (21:30 Tue 17 Feb to 10:00 Wed 18 Feb), area (western regions of the UAE), source and instruction match the English. The machine-translated Arabic description, however, adds a long advisory paragraph that is not in the English and repeats it three times. That paragraph introduces new protective actions: avoid going out except in extreme necessity, keep windows closed, check vehicles before driving, and follow official bulletins and avoid rumours. The English tells people to drive with caution, not to stay home, so the Arabic changes the protective action. The repetition also makes the text far too long. The drafter should remove the added text. A named Arabic reader must still approve the final Arabic.

objections.issue: The Arabic description adds protective actions that are not in the English: avoid going out except in extreme necessity, keep windows closed, and check your vehicle. The whole added paragraph is repeated three times. This changes the protective action (English: drive with extreme caution) and makes the Arabic much longer than the English and beyond typical alert length limits. This is the kind of material inaccuracy expected from unreviewed machine translation.
objections.fix: Delete everything after 'المصدر: المركز الوطني للأرصاد الجوية.' in the Arabic description, so it matches the English description exactly. Protective action should appear only in the instruction, as in the English. Have a named Arabic reader confirm the corrected text.
